about: D11-1, the muster (docs/design/war.md §14.1, §14.3; D-012 feudal armies; D-110). The branches of a realm's armed men, as data: the arm each belongs to (GD.ARMS key), the war map's troops it fills (GD.TROOPS codes, in order of preference) and the support companies it mans (GD.SUP keys), the weapon skills it uses, its ways of fighting, the aptitudes a muster-master prizes in it, what it needs, what it beats and loses to, its drills (war.md §14.2's families), duties in peace, missions and a way out. Read by src/war/9999955-muster (A.MUSTER). Drafted from docs/research/d11-military-branches.json, with conscript foot in place of the old call-up and the train and ships' companies added. Rank and unit words follow the one glossary (ranks, below; R14).

ways.shock: the shock: one great blow, knee to knee
ways.wall: standing in a rank: the wall that does not move
ways.press: the close press, blade to blade
ways.loose: loose order: harry, wheel and ride off
ways.shot: the shot: kill them before they reach you
ways.stealth: stealth: the silent march and the night
ways.steady: steadiness: the watch kept and the wall held

branches.name: The lances
branches.beats: archers in the open, loose foot, light horse caught standing
branches.loses: a set wall of spears, archers behind stakes, broken ground
duties: the tourney and the practice field
branches.wayOut: a knight's fee and a hall, or a grave in a field the charge did not cross
branches.desc: Knights and mounted men-at-arms: a few hundred armoured riders who win a battle in one moment or lose it. A horse, harness and birth open the door.

branches.name: The light horse
branches.beats: archers in the open, the baggage, a broken line
branches.loses: anything armoured and set, horse in close order
branches.wayOut: a horse of your own and a name on the border, or a fall in a ditch at a gallop
branches.desc: Riders in light harness who scout, raid, harry and pursue. They win by never fighting the whole army.

branches.name: The Scout Regiment
branches.beats: plans: they choose where, when and whether
branches.loses: any line that stands and fights
branches.wayOut: the realm's eyes, hated and needed; or a knife in the dark
branches.desc: The army's eyes: trackers, woodsmen and riders who go ahead, count the enemy, find the ford and come back. Tongues help.

branches.name: The spears
branches.beats: horse that charges a set wall
branches.loses: archers who shoot a wall that cannot move, armoured foot in the grind
branches.wayOut: a sergeant's stripe and a pension of bread; or a mound in a long field
branches.desc: Spears and pikes: the wall the army forms around. Anyone of size can be taught to hold a file; few are taught to hold it when the horses come.

branches.name: The men-at-arms on foot
branches.beats: spears and conscripts in the grind
branches.loses: archers they cannot catch, a flank turned
duties: the assault on a wall in a bad year
branches.wayOut: a captaincy, or a name among the men who went first through a breach
branches.desc: Armoured foot who win the grind: sword, axe and shield in the close press. A man who brings mail and can use a blade is wanted here.

branches.name: The bows
branches.beats: a wall that cannot move, horse that charges stakes
branches.loses: horse in the open, rain on the strings
branches.wayOut: a master of bowmen's place, or a hand that cannot draw any more
branches.desc: Bowmen in companies, behind stakes: they break charges and thin walls. A man who can draw a war bow is worth his bread from the first day.

branches.name: The crossbows
branches.beats: armour at short range, a wall that cannot move
branches.loses: horse that reaches them before the reload
branches.wayOut: a town's hire and a house by the gate, or a bolt the other way
branches.desc: Crossbowmen behind pavises: slow to load, but a bolt goes through mail. Patient men and men who keep a mechanism in order.

branches.name: The siege engineers
branches.loses: crossbows on a wall, a sally by night
branches.wayOut: a master engineer's name on a wall, or the mine that fell in
branches.desc: Masons, carpenters and miners under arms: they take walls, cross rivers and dig the camp. A trade is worth more here than a sword.

branches.name: The garrisons
branches.beats: an assault on a wall they know
branches.loses: hunger, a long siege and treachery
branches.wayOut: a castellan's keys, or a long life at a gate
branches.desc: The men who hold castles and town walls in peace and war: steady, older, known in the town.

branches.name: The train
branches.beats: hunger: an army marches on its bread
missions: find forage in a bare land
branches.wayOut: master of the train, a man the Generals cannot do without
branches.desc: Quartermasters, clerks and carters: bread, arrows and the wagon line. Numbers, letters and a trader's eye are worth more here than a strong arm.

branches.name: The ships' companies
branches.beats: ships, landings and a river crossing
branches.wayOut: a master's berth or a captain's deck, or the sea
branches.desc: Fighting men on ships and in harbours: boarding, rowing in stroke and the landing. Only a realm with a coast keeps them, and it wants men who know the sea.

branches.name: The household guard
branches.beats: anything that comes for their lord
branches.wayOut: a sworn man's land, or death at his lord's side
branches.desc: Sworn men of a lord's household, or the crown's royal knights: they guard their lord and stand at the banner. Birth, a patron or a famous deed opens the door.

branches.name: The elite orders
branches.wayOut: a Grand Master's chair, or a name on the order's wall
branches.desc: The few hundred men of the elite orders, who serve the crown and take the best of the whole kingdom by trial. Not entered at a muster: by their own trials.

branches.name: The hired companies
branches.beats: whoever they are paid to beat
duties: a town's walls for a season
branches.wayOut: a fortune, a captaincy-general, or the gallows
branches.desc: Free companies who fight for whoever pays, as long as he pays. Signed at a company's table, not a muster.

branches.name: The conscript foot
branches.beats: nothing, unless there are a great many of them
branches.wayOut: home when the need ends, or a transfer when someone wants you
branches.desc: Men taken by lot for a named need, raw and armed from their lord's store. No offers: the lot puts a man here, though aptitude is noticed in service.
